title: AI Ad Image Generator for Social Feed Ads | AIVideosUGC
description: Create square feed ad images from a product photo, with room to add a verified headline or price in Ads Manager or Canva before posting.
h1: AI Ad Image Generator for Facebook and Instagram Feeds
lead: Use this AI ad image generator to make a square product image for a Facebook or Instagram feed ad. Leave space around the product, then add your approved headline and price in Ads Manager or Canva.
secondary_keywords: square ad images for social media
AI images for paid social ads
intro: A feed ad gets only a moment to catch someone's eye while they scroll. Most of that work is done by the picture: a bright setting, a clear product and a bit of open space where your message can go. This tool takes one product photo and builds a square ad image around it, like a running shoe on a sunlit rock above a mountain lake.

It's made for shop owners and marketers who run ads on Facebook and Instagram and need new pictures often, since people stop noticing an image they've seen many times. Keep words out of the image itself. Add your headline, price or offer in Ads Manager, Canva or your usual design app, where you control spelling and layout, then compare the new ad with the one you're already running.

benefits.d: When an ad stops getting attention, give the same product a different setting and try again.
Ask for open sky, a plain wall or empty space at one side so your headline has somewhere to sit.
The item stays the focus, so people know what you're selling before they read anything.

steps.d: Use a clean shot of just the item, without packaging or other products crowding it.

steps.t: Describe the ad scene and its open space
steps.d: Pick a ready-made ad look or describe one, for example "running shoe on a rocky trail, lake behind, empty sky at the top."
Save the image, place your headline and price in your ad tool, and create a second version if you'd like another option to compare.

uses.d: Use the square image in a single-image ad and write your headline and offer in Ads Manager.
Run it as a sponsored post that sits naturally among the photos people already scroll past.
Make one image per product or per setting, then combine them into a carousel in your ad account.
Show people who browsed your shop a fresh look at the item they viewed, instead of the same store photo.

faq.q: Can the AI put my headline and price on the image?
faq.a: Add them yourself in Ads Manager, Canva or another design tool. AI-generated lettering can come out misspelled or garbled, and requests with a lot of text may be refused, so typing it yourself keeps prices and offers accurate.

faq.q: What size are the ad images?
faq.a: They're square by default, a shape that works in both Facebook and Instagram feeds.

faq.q: Can I create a few different ad images to compare?
faq.a: Yes, one at a time. Generate another image whenever you want a new option, with the cost shown before each one, then compare them in your ad account.

faq.q: Do I have to say my ad image was made with AI?
faq.a: Ad platforms set their own rules for AI-generated or edited images, and those rules change. Check the current policy for each platform you advertise on before your campaign goes live.

overview.h2: Design the picture around the message you will add
overview.d: A feed still has one job before the caption is read: make the product easy to spot. Ask for one clear subject, a visual contrast that separates it from the background, and a quiet area where your exact headline or offer can sit later. The image supplies the scene; your ad tool supplies the words.

overview.h2: Make versions that test a visual question
overview.d: Change one variable at a time—a pale kitchen versus a dark counter, a close crop versus a wider scene, or a product-only view versus a use moment. Keeping the product constant makes the comparison easier to understand when you place the files in your ad account.

input_guide.h2: Prepare a source for fast recognition

items.d: Use a source photo with one main product and no unrelated packages or props competing for the first glance.
Keep the full product visible when its silhouette matters; use a closer crop only when a texture or finish is the selling detail.
In the scene brief, request open sky, a plain wall, or a quiet tabletop on the side where your headline will go.
If a bundle is the offer, show the actual pieces together in the source rather than asking the scene to invent what is inside the box.
Leave words out of the generated scene; type the price, date, and promotion later in the ad editor.

The scene can leave a calm side or top area for your later headline, offer, or price.

fit.h2: A useful still for paid-social work

good.d: Products that can be recognized quickly from one strong angle and one clear scene.
Teams that want one product or setting per card while keeping a consistent visual treatment.
Stores that need a new visual for an item people have already seen in the catalog.

not_ideal.d: Use a design editor when the creative depends on several lines, exact legal text, or a detailed price grid.
Base claims about performance, ingredients, and dimensions on verified product details.

after_download.h2: Finish the ad in the place that runs it

items.d: Add headline, price, date, discount code, and any required wording in Ads Manager, Canva, or your normal editor.
Preview the creative where it will run and make sure the product and the reserved message area survive the placement crop.
Check the current rules for AI-generated or edited images before you publish the campaign.
